source_review.notes: Checked all seven official provider sources. Current SQS documentation supports max receive/redrive policy, type compatibility, redrive task/rate/permission behavior, new transport identity/enqueue time on redrive, interleaving, and standard-versus-FIFO retention clocks. Current Google Pub/Sub documentation supports subscription-scoped dead-letter topics, wrapper/source attributes, IAM dependence, and approximate best-effort maximum attempts. Current RabbitMQ documentation supports reject/expiry/max-length/delivery-limit triggers, routing/header history, cycles, and configuration-dependent dead-letter republishing safety. Current Azure Service Bus documentation supports DLQ subqueues, explicit inspection/settlement, application reasons, and lack of automatic cleanup. Pulsar 3.3 documentation supports version/subscription-scoped retry-letter and dead-letter behavior. The chapter treats every behavior as provider-specific rather than universal.

evidence: Checked logical message m, attempts a_i, fingerprint f(m), consumer c, subject version v, deadline D, effect IDs e_k(m), class k, case Q(c,m,r), occurrence epoch r, disposition d(m), rates lambda_d/mu_d, backlog L_d, time W_d, bytes b_d, and retention T_d for consistent domains.
Confirmed lifecycle arrows denote allowed operational transitions, not an automatically guaranteed provider state machine.
Confirmed backlog growth, Little's Law, and retained-byte formulas state stability/first-order assumptions and do not overclaim burst behavior.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Original logical identity remains distinct from provider delivery, dead-letter wrapper, redrive, and case identities.

evidence: Recomputed first 15-minute backlog as 150*15*60=135,000 messages.
Recomputed minute-15-to-45 net addition as (150-40)*30*60=198,000 and minute-45 backlog as 333,000.
Recomputed post-incident drain rate as 40-8=32/s and drain time as 333,000/32=10,406.25 seconds=173.4375 minutes, about 2h53m26s.
Recomputed Example 9 backlog growth as (80-50)*3,600=108,000 messages/hour.
Counted ten worked examples and five exercise-answer pairs.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Scenario computations intentionally exclude repeat failures, key ordering, approvals, bursts, and downstream headroom.

evidence: Constructed acknowledge-before-dead-letter-capture trace proving possible loss and capture-before-ack trace proving possible duplicate cases without idempotent identity.
Confirmed atomic provider movement or an idempotent durable application case bridges the source/DLQ dual-write only within named failure and retention assumptions.
Constructed poison-gap trace proving removal can let later subject versions overtake and requires keyed blocking/version policy.
Constructed timeout-after-external-success trace proving redrive must reconcile stable effect identity before retry.
Constructed settle-before-disposition trace proving a case can vanish without accountable closure.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The proof establishes accountable capture/disposition, not automatic safe business recovery.

Reviewed provider approximate/reset counts, wrapping, new transport IDs, interleaving, forwarding failure, cycles, routing, retention-clock differences, manual inspection, cancellation, and region/restore behavior.

Reviewed duplicate forwarding, same-ID fingerprint conflict, source/DLQ parity, order holes, batch/live interaction, stale authorization, dedup expiry, mass redrive, partial completion, repeat failure, and terminal dispositions.
Reviewed hostile compressed/rendered content, secret/PII leakage, cross-tenant enumeration, unauthorized destination/edit/redrive, KMS/IAM failure, key rotation, and retention/deletion.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Coverage spans semantic, transport, capture, storage, ordering, external, regional, operational, lifecycle, privacy, and adversarial boundaries.

evidence: Confirmed original application ID/fingerprint/source/order/consumer provenance survives provider wrapping and redrive transport identity changes.
Confirmed retry/redrive selection depends on class, age, deadline, authorization, effect uncertainty, compatibility, idempotency horizon, order, and capacity—not count alone.
Confirmed provider source removal is paired with durable capture/case evidence and forwarding/case parity is observable.
Confirmed redrive is canary/rate limited, preserves logical/effect IDs, prevents loops, and stops on repeat failure or invariant drift.
Confirmed provider deletion/settlement follows a durable verified success or authorized terminal disposition.
invariant_checking.notes: A DLQ is consistently modeled as unresolved governed work rather than successful processing.

evidence: Reviewed accountable-capture proof and confirmed each premise—durable move/bridge, unique case/fingerprint, retention, and settle-after-disposition—is necessary.
Reviewed rate model and confirmed positive lambda_d-mu_d produces unbounded backlog absent source arrest or increased safe resolution.
Reviewed redrive argument and confirmed repair alone is insufficient without compatibility, idempotency/effect reconciliation, order/deadline/auth, capacity, and verification gates.
Reviewed active-region/payment answer and confirmed eventual case replication does not prove single external effect.
proof_review.notes: Counterexamples constrain the claim to named systems, horizons, and business-effect mechanisms.

evidence: Confirmed proof sketch explicitly distinguishes accountable capture from safe recovery.
Confirmed SQS, Pub/Sub, RabbitMQ, Azure Service Bus, and Pulsar behaviors are attributed and mode/version scoped.
Confirmed application recommendations, domain dispositions, provider facts, algebra/rate models, and empirical obligations use distinct language.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Provider names do not imply interchangeable DLQ semantics.

evidence: All seven official sources were retrieved or checked on 2026-09-02; Pulsar reference is pinned to 3.3 and RabbitMQ to the documented next/current path.
All numeric rates, durations, counts, and canary sizes are labeled worked-example or exercise scenarios, not defaults/SLOs.

Actual provider forwarding durability, IAM/KMS, retention clocks, message transformations, safe redrive rate, downstream capacity, case storage, resolution staffing, and business invariants remain explicit integration/load/fault evidence obligations.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No production broker, queue, case store, payment provider, region topology, or incident process was empirically assessed.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed dead-letter lifecycle, failure taxonomy, retry/hold/quarantine distinctions, failure envelope, provider semantics, durable capture, ordering, backlog/retention, diagnosis/repair, controlled redrive, dispositions, security, and end-to-end verification as one coherent recovery system.

practitioner_review.notes: Checked implementability through normalized case identity/state, safe indexed evidence, provider policy/IAM validation, forwarding parity, keyed gaps, SLO/capacity dashboards, clustering/reproduction, eligibility gates, canary/rate-limited redrive, automated stops, durable disposition, least-privilege tooling, probes, and reconciliation.

pedagogical_review.notes: The module begins by separating transport dead lettering from business resolution, builds classification and evidence, then covers provider semantics, operational recovery, controlled redrive, closure, and security. Ten examples isolate distinct failure surfaces; five exercises progress from classification and schema through queue arithmetic, mass redrive, and multi-region payments with complete answers.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
